The role and mission
Your mission is to find out what's technically possible, and to build enough to prove it. You'll be as much an AI engineer as a software engineer, because much of what the Lab builds has AI at its core.
"Lead" means you're the senior engineer in the Lab's core team, so the technical calls are yours. You set the technical direction across our ideas, and you write a lot of the code yourself. That also means you drive your own work and your own learning. You're part of the core team led by the Director of Product Lab, and you report directly to the Director of Technology in Schibsted's Product organisation.
The role grows with the Lab. You start with no direct reports and your hands in the code. As Product Lab grows, you'll also help shape how we build technical teams around successful bets, and strengthen the engineering craft and culture of the Lab. Over time, that can include people management.
What you will do
Assess new product ideas quickly for technical feasibility, cost and risk, and give a clear recommendation to stop, continue or scale them.
Build and ship early prototypes and experiments, using whatever mix of code, AI tools, APIs and Schibsted platforms gets us to real user learning fastest.
Build new product experiences with AI at the core, using language models, agents and retrieval over our journalism, rather than adding AI to the products we already have.
Make architecture and technology choices that fit how mature each idea is, and know what a scrappy prototype needs to become a solid, scalable product.
Work closely with product, design and editorial colleagues, and connect Lab ideas with the engineering, data, AI and platform teams across Schibsted.
Coach the engineers who join our teams, many of them for a few weeks or months from other parts of Schibsted, so they take new skills back to their own teams.
Who we are looking for
You're a product-minded engineer and builder who thrives at the earliest and most uncertain stage of a product. You enjoy finding out whether something can be built, finding the fastest credible way to test it, and moving on once the important questions have answers.
You're pragmatic rather than precious about technology. Sometimes the right answer is solid engineering. Sometimes it's an API, an AI-generated prototype, or something held together just well enough to test an idea. You know the difference, and you know when it's time to rebuild. So this isn't a role for someone who wants to build everything from scratch, or to optimise for production quality from day one.
We believe you bring
Significant experience building digital and AI products as a software engineer, tech lead or similar senior role, and you're still strongly hands-on.
Hands-on experience building on AI models. You've shipped products or features built on language models, such as agents, retrieval or generated content. You know how to measure whether the output is good enough, and what it costs to run.
Broad technical skills across front end, back end, APIs and data, so you can build a whole prototype yourself.
An AI-native way of working. Coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex are part of how you build every day. You can show us how you use them, where they help and where they don't.
Experience taking products from prototype to production, with the judgement to make pragmatic trade-offs when information is limited.
A track record of stopping things. You've recommended stopping a feature, a system or a product you believed in when the evidence went against it. And you can tell us how you did it.

Schibsted | Oslo, Bergen or Stockholm (hybrid)
We built our own dynamic paywall and offer engine. Now we need to make it better, understand what works, and bring it to more brands.
We're looking for a Data Scientist who enjoys building models, testing ideas and finding out whether the results actually make a difference. You'll work alongside experienced data scientists, analysts and engineers, with opportunities to take ownership of your work and grow your skills along the way.
Why this work matters
Our democracies depend on independent journalism, and that is our business. Independent journalism needs readers who choose to pay for it.
Our job in Subscription Data Enablement is to understand those readers well enough to offer them the right thing at the right time, and to leave them alone when we shouldn't bother them.
Direct relationships with readers and digital profitability are how Schibsted measures success. Your models sit right in the middle of both.
Who we are
We are the data and analytics team for Schibsted's Subscription business in Norway and Sweden: analysts, data engineers, an ML engineer and data scientists.
We work with brands such as VG, Aftenposten, Aftonbladet, Svenska Dagbladet, Bergens Tidende and E24. Our models already cover churn, renewal, segmentation and engagement. The dynamic paywall and offer engine is the newest addition to the family.
It is also a good test of how we work. The Dynamic Paywall project has many moving parts and competing priorities, and it needs people from data, product, tech, business and editorial teams in the same room.
A consultant who recently worked with us said that, despite technically being a consultant, they "never really felt like one". They described a team where everyone brings different expertise, ideas get challenged, debates are healthy, and we don't always agree, but there is "always mutual respect" and a shared goal of finding the best way forward.
We want you to feel the same way about us a year from now.
What you will do
Make our paywall smarter. Develop and improve the models behind our dynamic paywall and offers: who sees which offer, and when. Propensity, recommender and offer optimisation problems are all in scope.
Find out what works. Design, run and analyse experiments with our brands, and report the results as they are, including what they don’t prove. Uplift modelling and causal inference are welcome tools here.
Build models that get used. Take models from notebook to production with our data scientists and engineers: feature engineering, training, evaluation, testing, and monitoring once they’re live. We work with tools such as Snowflake, MLflow and Streamlit.
Make the results understandable. Explain findings to commercial colleagues with clear analysis and dashboards where they help.
Improve how we work. Bring ideas on modelling, tooling and MLOps as more brands come on board, including how AI can make our own work easier.
Ask good questions. Including “does this actually make us money?” when someone needs to.
What you bring
Python or R and SQL, used to analyse data and build models.
Hands-on experience developing and evaluating machine learning models, and an understanding of what it takes to run them in production.
A solid foundation in statistics and experimentation, including hypothesis testing and A/B tests.
The ability to explain your work to people who don’t speak ML, and the curiosity to learn from people who know the business better than you do.
How we work
We follow a short list of team principles, and we mean them: be curious and keep learning, deliver quality together, design collaboratively, help early and ask early, share generously, have fun and stay open.
In practice, that means Show n Tell and Friday data talks every other week, a monthly hack day, and an expectation that you ask for help before you’re stuck, not after. We also encourage sitting in on newsroom meetings. It’s hard to build a good model of what readers value without knowing what the newsrooms think is important.
What you can expect from us
Real ML problems, with models that influence decisions across some of the Nordics’ best-known news brands.
Experienced colleagues to learn from, and room to take ownership of your work.
Time and space to learn, experiment and share ideas.
The practical bits
Location: Oslo, Bergen or Stockholm. Hybrid.
Employee terms and benefits follow Schibsted’s standards in your country, and we are happy to go through the details with you in the process.
The team is spread across Norway and Sweden, so some days are on video.
Working language: English
We welcome applications from people with different experiences and career paths, and we focus on the skills and potential you bring.
Apply
Send your CV and a few lines about a data science or machine learning project you've worked on. What problem were you trying to solve, what was your contribution, and what did you learn?
It doesn't have to be a model you took all the way to production. We're interested in how you think and what you've learned from doing the work.
No long cover letter needed.
We'll keep you informed throughout the process and let you know the outcome of your application.
Deadline: November 6th 2026
Questions? Contact Johanna Haglund Lindqvist, Head of Data Science & Data Engineering.
About Schibsted
Schibsted is the largest news provider in the Nordics, with brands such as VG, Aftonbladet, TV4, MTV, Aftenposten, Svenska Dagbladet and Podme. Every day we inform, engage and entertain millions of people across Sweden, Norway and Finland. Since 1839, trust has been our foundation.

title: Korrespondent i Russland
description:
Aftenposten søker ny korrespondent i Russland med base i Moskva. Vi ser etter en journalist med gode kontaktskapende evner som kan formidle både russernes hverdag og det storpolitiske spillet.
Vi søker en journalist som er analytisk og nysgjerrig. Du har stor interesse for internasjonale forhold, og du har trolig fulgt spesielt nøye med på Russland i en periode. Det er en stor fordel om du behersker russisk.
I tillegg har du stor arbeidskapasitet og er flink til å forklare komplekse saksforhold så alle forstår dem.
Aftenposten har en topp moderne leilighet som ligger nær kontoret vi leier i en veldig sentral del av den russiske hovedstaden.
Korrespondenten blir fast ansatt i Aftenposten. Vi kan diskutere lengden på korrespondentperioden. Etter endt periode vil den som ansettes, bli en del av Aftenpostens redaksjon i Oslo.
En ansettelse forutsetter at søkeren får innvilget visum og presseakkreditering i Russland.
Kan det være noe for deg? Ta kontakt for en uforpliktende samtale.
Søknader blir vurdert fortløpende frem til 7. november 2026
Spørsmål om stillingen?
Ta kontakt med utenrikssjef John Hultgren på telefon [phone removed] eller e-post [email removed] eller klubbleder Kristjan Molstad, tlf. [phone removed]/ [email removed].
Om oss
Hundretusener av nordmenn stoler hver dag på at Aftenposten gir dem troverdig, engasjerende og innsiktsfull dekning av det viktigste som skjer i Norge og verden. Vi har som ambisjon å være den foretrukne kvalitetsavisen for samfunnsengasjerte mennesker i hele landet – og et ledende digitalt mediehus.
Aftenposten har utviklet seg fra å være Norges største papiravis til å bli en av landets fremste digitale medieaktører, med sterk vekst i digitale abonnementer og en stadig voksende portefølje av podkaster og nye produkter. For å lykkes må vi være best på journalistikk, teknologiutvikling og kommersialisering – og vi jobber på tvers av fagmiljøer for å skape morgendagens mediehus.
Journalistikken, produktutviklingen og det kommersielle arbeidet vårt er prisbelønt – både nasjonalt og internasjonalt. Ambisjonene for fremtiden er store.
Aftenposten er en del av Schibsted, et ledende nordisk mediekonsern med andre sterke merkevarer som VG, Bergens Tidende, Aftonbladet, Svenska Dagbladet og TV4. Det gir oss kraft, kompetanse og muligheter til å tenke større.

title: Senior Data Lead - Product
description:
About the position
Schibsted Media builds news products that more than 6 million people across the Nordics use every day. Data is at the heart of building products that people love, and we are building a modern data foundation that supports smarter personalization, user engagement, and monetization across our media brands.
We are now hiring a Senior Data Lead to join us. This is a new role, created as our data teams have grown and matured. We now want to take the next step towards a shared way of working, with common standards and best practice that hold across domains, disciplines and brands, and we are looking for someone to lead that work.
As Senior Data Lead you work directly alongside our Director of Data, with wide influence across analytics, data engineering and data science. Our Product Data teams span three domains. User covers the user lifecycle, Content covers the lifecycle of the news content we produce, and Performance works directly with our media brands. Your role spans all three, setting shared direction and standards that help teams stay aligned and move faster with data.
What you will do
You will be accountable for Product Data as a discipline, and lead the cross-product data initiatives that no single domain can own.
Set the direction. Together with the Director of Data, define technical and analytical direction across our data domains, and be a point of reference for analysts, data engineers and data scientists.
Shape how we work. Build our operating model and one shared playbook of standards, guidelines and reusable patterns, covering how data products are owned, documented and kept reliable. You do this together with lead analysts, engineers and product owners, who each drive a practice area such as metrics and KPIs, data products, engineering or experimentation.
Lead cross-product initiatives. Lead a small number of data initiatives that span several domains and brands, such as shared KPIs and user segments across our products.
Improve how we build with AI. Explore and scale new ways of using AI across data work, from better tools for analysts and engineers to agents, and set the quality bar for AI-produced analysis. Make sure our data is ready to power AI product features.
Partner with Schibsted's central Data teams. Work closely with our central Data and AI teams on governance, data architecture and shared standards. Bring in Product's needs and expectations, and turn shared decisions into how we work in Product.
Grow senior people. Coach and develop senior and lead individual contributors across all three disciplines, without line management.
What we're looking for:
You bring deep expertise in at least one of analytics, data engineering or data science, and enough fluency in the others to be credible across all three. We don't expect anyone to be an expert in everything below.
At the core, you have
7+ years of experience in analytics, data engineering or data science, including several years in senior or lead roles with influence across teams.
Experience building shared ways of working, standards and best practice across several teams.
Experience designing metrics and KPIs that hold across brands, products or markets.
Strong SQL and data modelling skills, with hands-on experience of dbt and a cloud warehouse such as Snowflake.
Strong skills in Python or R.
Applied experience using AI and LLM tooling in analytical or engineering work.
Clear technical writing, ideally with experience of architecture decision records (ADRs).
Strong judgement about scope and priorities. You can decline or redirect work, including valuable work, so that the most important things get done.
Depth in some of these is a strong plus
Data mesh and data product practice, such as domain ownership, data contracts, service levels and documentation.
Data governance, data quality and privacy under GDPR.
Experiment design and causal inference, including quasi-experimental methods and holdouts.
ML and AI methods, deep enough to set quality and evaluation standards for others' work.
It's also a plus if you have
Fluent Swedish or Norwegian. You will work closely with editorial and brand stakeholders in both markets.
Experience from media, or from translating data work for executive and board-level audiences.
We encourage applicants from all backgrounds, experiences, and identities to apply, even if you don't meet every requirement. What matters most is your motivation and potential.
Our tech stack:
Data platform: AWS, Snowflake
Transformation and orchestration: dbt, Airflow
Programming and scripting: Python, SQL, R
Exploration and delivery: Amplitude, Superset, Streamlit, Kilkaya
Tracking and events: Pulse (in-house tracking), Kafka
Who you are
You lead through influence. You build alignment in groups that don't report to you, explain the why behind a standard, and are comfortable holding an outcome while someone else does the work. You write clearly, because much of what you produce has to work without you in the room. And you have good judgement about scope: you make a call, document your reasoning, and say no when something belongs elsewhere.
Why we enjoy working here:
At Schibsted, we value openness, curiosity, and collaboration. You'll be part of a diverse, inclusive workplace that encourages bold thinking and continuous learning. Our work directly supports public interest journalism, and we take that responsibility seriously.
Whether you're enabling better content decisions, driving user personalization, or shaping experimentation at scale, your contributions will help shape the future of digital media in the Nordics.
You will be joining a collaborative, impact-driven team that works across disciplines like technology, product, and editorial. We believe in structured yet flexible ways of working, balancing clear ownership with strong teamwork. Curiosity, openness, and a drive to create value through data are at the heart of how we operate. We support each other, celebrate continuous learning, and are passionate about turning complex challenges into meaningful solutions for our users and brands.
Application process:
Please apply for this position by sharing your CV with us and a letter of motivation. English is our corporate language, but you are welcome to write it in Swedish or Norwegian. Selection of candidates takes place on an ongoing basis during the process.

title: Data Engineer in Data Product Engineering
description:
If you choose to apply, please read the job ad in full and include a short cover letter. We are most interested in hearing from the real you, so we encourage authentic applications written in your own words.
The opportunity in a nutshell
Interested in combining hands-on data engineering with close collaboration across the business? This role could be a good fit for someone with 4+ years of experience who enjoys building reliable data products and working with others to make them useful.
Role: Join as a Data Engineer in our Data Product Engineering team within Schibsted's Data & AI organization, where we build reliable, well-governed, and scalable data products used across Finance, HR, Product, Subscription, and other parts of the business.
Core tools and practices: Our everyday toolkit includes SQL and Python as core languages, together with Snowflake, dbt, Airflow, AWS, Terraform, and Git, supported by solid engineering practices around testing, documentation, CI/CD, and version control.
Company: Schibsted is home to some of the most established and widely used media brands in the Nordics, including Aftenposten, VG, Svenska Dagbladet, Aftonbladet, E24, Bergens Tidende, and Stavanger Aftenblad. Across our broader Data & AI focus, data, analytics, and AI help us build better products, support smarter decisions, and create value across those newsrooms and businesses.
Location: This role is based in Oslo or Stockholm. We work in a hybrid setup, which means this is not a fully remote role, and candidates need to reside in Sweden or Norway and be able to work from one of our offices at least 2 days a week.
Why this role: You will join a relatively new team with room to contribute, learn, and help shape how we work as we continue to build trusted data products across Schibsted.
Sounds like your kind of role? Read on
Who are you?
We are looking for someone with a solid foundation in data engineering who is also excited by the opportunity to keep learning, deepen their craft, and grow together with the team.
You have around 4+ years of experience in data engineering or a closely related role, with a track record of building reliable data solutions in production environments.
Strong SQL skills are important, along with a solid understanding of data modeling, data warehousing, and how to design data products that are useful, trustworthy, and maintainable.
You can write and debug SQL and Python yourself at a strong professional level. AI-assisted tools are welcome, but this role requires solid enough fundamentals to solve everyday engineering problems without depending totally on them.
On the Python side, we are looking for good software engineering fundamentals, including the ability to structure maintainable applications and apply object-oriented design principles where appropriate.
You have hands-on experience with dbt in production environments and solid working knowledge of the wider toolkit we use, including Airflow, Snowflake, AWS, Terraform, Git, and Python and / or similar tools.
You will likely enjoy this role if you are comfortable making pragmatic technical decisions in environments where requirements evolve and not everything is fully defined upfront.
You care about engineering quality and can contribute to practices around testing, documentation, observability, governance, and cost-efficient pipeline design.
Clear communication matters just as much as technical strength. We value people who can work well with both technical and non-technical stakeholders, explain tradeoffs clearly, and contribute positively to team collaboration and knowledge sharing.
What's the job like?
As a Data Engineer, your job is to help us build data as a product, not just pipelines that move data from one place to another. You will create robust data models, improve the reliability and scalability of our pipelines, and help shape the engineering practices that make our data products trusted and reusable across Schibsted Media.
What you will be expected to do
Collaborate with stakeholders to translate business needs into pragmatic, well-scoped data solutions.
Design, build, and maintain reliable pipelines and transformations in Snowflake, dbt, Airflow, and Python.
Develop scalable data models that support analytics, reporting, and future AI use cases.
Improve technical quality through testing, documentation, monitoring, and maintainable engineering practices.
Contribute to good architectural and implementation decisions across the team.
Contribute through code reviews, pairing, and knowledge sharing within the team.
Work closely with adjacent platform and Data & AI teams to align on standards, dependencies, and shared ways of working.
What success looks like
Success in this role means growing into a confident contributor who understands our data landscape, ways of working, and stakeholder needs. Over time, that includes contributing across a mix of smaller support tasks through our weekly rotation as well as larger pieces of work, helping build reliable pipelines and data models, and developing the judgment to deliver pragmatic solutions together with the team. Depending on your experience and the needs of the work, that can mean contributing as part of a team or taking the lead on a project.
Why join us?
You will join a team that is still shaping its ways of working, which means there is real room to contribute, learn, and grow.
You will work on data products with visible impact across Schibsted, supporting both technical and non-technical users in domains such as Product, Subscription, Finance, and HR.
You will be part of a company whose work matters in everyday life across the Nordics, helping support trusted media brands through better data, analytics, and AI capabilities.
You will work in an international environment with strong trust, autonomy, and good opportunities for learning through engineering communities and collaboration across Data & AI.
You will join a team that enjoys solving challenging problems, wants to build high-quality data products, and cares about the people they work with.
Got your attention? Let us hear from you!
The application period closes on 28 September 2026. We review applications on a rolling basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

title: Fullstack utvikler, VG X
description:
VG X er et lite, tverrfaglig startup på innsiden av VG som ble satt i gang høsten 2024 og består av de skarpeste hodene vi har klart å oppdrive innenfor journalistikk, teknologi, design, forretnings- og produktutvikling.
Oppdraget er å gjenoppfinne nyheter for en ny generasjon lesere som synes at dagens løsninger gjør det for vanskelig å holde seg oppdatert. Vi skal strekke strikken og gå radikalt til verks rundt hvordan VG kan fungere i fremtiden, og utfordre alle områder av dagens rigg.
Nå søker vi etter to fullstack-utviklere som vil være med på å utvikle fremtidens versjon av VG.
Mer om prosjektet i denne artikkelen fra Medier 24:
https://www.m24.no/kunstig-intelligens-medieinnovasjon-rolf-sonstelie/dette-er-vgs-radikale-nye-prosjekt-vg-x/886860
Presentasjon av Gard Steiro om hva VG X er, og hvorfor det er viktig for VG:
https://youtu.be/8Q7zR7duNro?si=ju5zFVeqszJsoEN2&t=620
Om rollen
Som utvikler i VG X får du en helt sentral rolle i utviklingen av fremtidens VG. Du vil jobbe hånd i hånd med alle fagområder for å gå raskt fra idé til noe vi faktisk tester ute i produktet. Vi ser etter deg som bryr deg om helheten: at det blir en god brukeropplevelse, at det er teknisk solid, og ikke minst at det faktisk løser et reelt brukerbehov.
Dette er ikke en rolle hvor du skal trene opp egne AI-modeller og bruke mye maskinlæring. Vi bruker eksisterende APIer og verktøy for å skape nye produktopplevelser.
Du vil blant annet:
Bygge løsninger med tett kobling mot AI-funksjonalitet, som f.eks personalisering, RAG og generering av innhold.
Designe og bygge agent-workflows og orkestrering av LLM-kall som løser konkrete brukerbehov.
Integrere backend-tjenester, API-er og datalagring for AI-, data-flyt og brukerdata.
Bryne deg på noe tyngre tekniske problemer som å analysere, gruppere og strukturere data for å bygge en datamodell som underbygger behovet til produktet.
Eksperimentere raskt med nye brukeropplevelser, fra prototype til test med reelle brukere.
Bidra til teknisk arkitektur og valg sammen med resten av teamet.
Jobbe tverrfaglig og produktnært. Du er med i diskusjonen om hva vi bygger, ikke bare hvordan.
Teknologier vi bruker
React
React Native
Python
Node
Typescript
MongoDB, PostgreSQL
Firebase, Supabase, Kubernetes, AWS, SQS/SNS
OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini
Du må ikke kjenne til alt dette fra dag én, men det hjelper å ha kjennskap til disse eller noe tilsvarende. Du bør være komfortabel med å sette deg inn en bred stack og ha en mening om hvordan ting burde se ut fremover.
Vi ser etter deg som
Er kreativ og tenker nytt. Du blir ikke fastlåst i “sånn gjør vi det alltid”.
Har noen års erfaring som fullstack-utvikler. Vi er mer interessert i potensial, nysgjerrighet og evne enn antall år.
Har jobbet med bruk av generativ AI i produkter. Agenter, workflows, prompting og orkestrering av LLM-kall.
Liker å bryne deg på tekniske utfordringer.
Er AI-native, men forstår at det først og fremst handler om å bygge gode produkter og solide tekniske løsninger. AI er verktøyet, ikke målet.
Er nær målgruppen vår i hvordan du selv bruker teknologi og nyheter, og har gode instinkter for hva som funker for denne generasjonen.
Liker å samarbeide tett og tverrfaglig med design, produkt og domenefolk, ikke bare andre utviklere.
Er nysgjerrig og engasjert utover eget fagfelt.
Er en sosial lagspiller
Kommuniserer tydelig og presist, både på norsk og engelsk, og kan forklare tekniske valg til folk uten teknisk bakgrunn.
Det du får i VG X
En viktig rolle i utviklingen av fremtidens VG
Innovasjonsmuskler: En fristilt «startup» på innsiden av VG, med ressursene og innholdet til Schibsted Media i ryggen.
AI-først kultur: Du får bruke de nyeste verktøyene, og vi investerer i at du skal være best på det.
Gøy, ungt og høykompetent team: Jobb med de beste folkene på tvers av tech, innhold, business og design, der vi hjelper hverandre.
VG og Schibsted
VG er Norges største destinasjon for nyheter, underholdning og digitale opplevelser. Som en del av Schibsted Media, er vi med i et økosystem som når ut til millioner av mennesker hver eneste dag.
I VG X jobber vi i grenselandet mellom journalistikk, teknologi og det uante. Vi er de som får lov til å feile, sånn at resten av huset kan vinne. Her får du kolleger som har vunnet de tyngste prisene for journalistikk, som koder algoritmer i verdensklasse, og som brenner for å leve i et informert, velfungerende, demokratisk samfunn.

title: Application Security Engineer
description:
Help protect the technology behind some of the Nordics' most important news organisations.
At Schibsted, cybersecurity is about more than protecting systems and applications. It's also about protecting journalism, the people behind it, and the technology that makes independent news accessible to millions of people.
We're looking for an Application Security Engineer to join our cybersecurity team in Stockholm or Oslo. This is a great opportunity for someone at the beginning of their cybersecurity career who wants to develop their technical skills, gain experience across a wide range of security challenges, and work closely with developers to build safer products.
First, a little about us
Schibsted is one of the leading media groups in the Nordics, home to well-known news brands including Aftonbladet, Svenska Dagbladet, VG and Aftenposten.
Every day, millions of people turn to our news organisations to stay informed, understand the world around them, and access independent journalism.
Behind these brands is a large and diverse technology organisation, building and maintaining the digital products, platforms and infrastructure that make all of this possible.
And with that comes an interesting security challenge.
Our news brands are highly visible, and the threats we face go beyond those of a typical corporate environment. From protecting applications and user data to safeguarding journalists and ensuring uninterrupted access to news, cybersecurity plays an important role in keeping our journalism accessible and independent.
That's where you come in.
What you'll be working on
As an Application Security Engineer, you'll help strengthen the security of our applications and digital products across Schibsted.
You'll be part of a cybersecurity team working across Sweden and Norway, collaborating with developers, architects and engineering teams throughout the organisation.
A big part of your job will be identifying vulnerabilities and security risks. But finding an issue is only the beginning.
You'll also work with the teams responsible for our products to understand the problem, find practical solutions, and help make sure vulnerabilities actually get resolved.
Since Schibsted is a large organisation with many different brands, products and technologies, no two challenges will necessarily look the same. You'll have the opportunity to learn from experienced colleagues, explore different technologies and gradually take on more responsibility as you develop your skills.
Some of the things you'll do:
Help identify and assess security vulnerabilities in our applications and digital products.
Work directly with developers and engineering teams to understand and remediate security issues.
Participate in security assessments and help integrate security practices throughout the software development lifecycle.
Support teams in understanding security risks and finding practical solutions.
Work with application security tools and contribute to improving our processes and ways of working.
Share knowledge and collaborate with colleagues across the organisation to strengthen security awareness.
Contribute to building a stronger security culture where security becomes a natural part of how we develop products.
Who we're looking for
You might be at the beginning of your cybersecurity career, with some hands-on experience in application security, penetration testing or a related technical field. Perhaps you've recently graduated, worked in your first security role, or developed your skills through technical projects.
What matters most to us is your technical curiosity, your willingness to learn, and your interest in understanding how applications can be made more secure.
We'd love to hear from you if you have:
Some practical experience with application security, penetration testing or related security work, whether through employment, internships or personal projects.
An understanding of common application vulnerabilities, such as those covered by the OWASP Top 10, and how they can be mitigated.
Familiarity with application security testing tools, such as Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP or similar.
A basic understanding of modern software development practices, web technologies and how applications are built.
An interest in assessing security risks and finding practical ways to address them.
The ability to explain technical concepts clearly and an interest in collaborating with developers and other teams.
Experience with cloud environments, infrastructure security, threat modelling or secure software development is also valuable, but not a requirement.
We're not expecting you to know everything from day one. We're looking for someone who's proactive, collaborative and eager to develop their skills. Someone who doesn't just want to identify security problems, but enjoys working with others to solve them.
Why join us?
Work that matters. The technology you help protect supports independent journalism and news organisations that play an important role in society.
Interesting security challenges. You'll work across a diverse technology landscape, with different products, engineering teams and security needs.
An opportunity to grow. You'll have the chance to learn from experienced cybersecurity colleagues, develop your technical expertise and gain hands-on experience with security challenges across a large technology organisation.
A role that combines technology and people. You'll get to dive into technical security challenges while building relationships and helping teams improve how they work.
Room to make an impact. Even early in your career, you'll have the opportunity to contribute not only to individual security improvements, but also to how we approach application security across Schibsted.
If this sounds like the kind of challenge you'd enjoy, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Leder for krim (vikariat)
description:
Om stillingen
VG søker teamleder til krimgruppa på nyhetsavdelingen i et seks måneders vikariat. I denne rollen blir du en viktig del av arbeidet med å styrke vår krimdekning og videreutvikle VG for fremtiden. Vi ser etter deg som ønsker å bidra til mer unik journalistikk og vinne nyhetskampene, med leserne i fokus. Du blir en del av nyhetsledelsen og får muligheten til god faglig utvikling.
Arbeidsoppgaver
Du vil ha ansvar for VGs krimdekning og jobbe tett med de øvrige lederne på nyhet. Stillingen innebærer at du tar strategisk ansvar for krimfeltet, følger opp medarbeiderne dine og at du aktivt bidrar med faglig innspill, utvikling og forbedringer i det daglige arbeidet. Du får også lederansvaret for Krimpodden.
Hvem vi søker
Vi søker deg som har et stort hjerte for krimjournalistikken, gode lederegenskaper og som trives i et miljø der tempoet er høyt og kravene til nøyaktighet er store. Du har sterkt nyhetsinstinkt, god vurderingsevne, kommuniserer tydelig og samarbeider godt med andre. Erfaring fra kildearbeid, jus og krimfeltet er en fordel. Kun fast ansatte i VG kan søke.
Vilkår
Stillingen er et vikariat i seks måneder. Stillingen er på dagtid, men det må påregnes arbeid på kveld/i helgen når nyhetsbildet krever det. Vi vurderer kandidater fortløpende, og stillingen kan bli besatt før søknadsfristen.
Kontakt
Har du spørsmål om stillingen, kontakt leder for nyhetsavdelingen, Eva-Therese Loo Grøttum. For spørsmål om tariff eller arbeidsvilkår, ta kontakt med klubbleder Hanna Haug Røset eller administrasjonssjef Andreas Nielsen.
Mediehuset VG er en del av mediekonsernet Schibsted og leverer nyheter, underholdning og nyttestoff på digitale flater i flere formater, samt utgir papiravis.
VG skal være primærdestinasjon for nyheter, sport og underholdning i Norge. VG har som mål hver dag å sette dagsorden for både det folkelige og det offisielle nyhetsbildet i Norge. VG har den største leserdekningen av norske mediehus og når daglig rundt 2 millioner lesere gjennom papir-, nett- og mobilutgaven.
I VG er mangfold nødvendig for å lykkes! Vi mener at mennesker med ulik bakgrunn og erfaring, sammen løser oppgaver på en bedre måte. Vi vil ha et arbeidsmiljø med like muligheter for folk med ulik seksuell legning, bakgrunn, nasjonalitet, alder, kjønn og for dem med en funksjonsnedsetting. Målet vårt er at VG som arbeidsplass skal representere befolkningen vi lager produkter og innhold for. Vi oppfordrer alle kvalifiserte kandidater til å søke.

title: Product Manager - Data Analytics
description:
📍 Oslo / Bergen / Bodø
💰 Salary: 1.150.000 - 1.300.000 NOK/year
🌍 Why this role matters
Four years ago, Aidn was just an idea. Today, we are the market leader in the municipal healthcare sector. As Aidn matures from startup to industry leader, we will do more than offer a great product. We will become the healthcare platform that elevates the entire ecosystem.
At Aidn, we are building the next generation of health technology for Norwegian municipalities. Analytical data sits at the core of that value proposition, through built-for-purpose analytical user interfaces. We have won a large share of the Norwegian market, and these municipalities are now being onboarded to Aidn, which makes reliable, well-structured data and insight more important than ever.
We believe that better decisions create better care – Aidn Analytics gives the people running, delivering, and building health and care services the insight to make good decisions and prepare for the challenges of tomorrow.
🔧 What you’ll be working on
In this role, you’ll own the product direction for Aidn Analytics, working closely with a design lead and tech lead in a product Trio. Together, you’ll discover the right problems to solve, test ideas, and follow their impact.
Your core responsibilities will include:
Setting a product direction: Setting the vision, strategy, and roadmap for Aidn Analytics, and keeping it connected to Aidn's product vision and real municipal needs.
Drive the transformation to distributed ownership: Define the operating model, golden paths, and governance together with domain teams, and enable them to develop and own their data products.
Own prioritisation across the data platform, analytics capabilities, and the overall Aidn Analytics user and developer experience.
Lead by example on being data-driven: Define success metrics, use data in your own decisions, and help Aidn and the municipalities do the same.
Building and learning with AI: Use AI tools systematically throughout your work; analyze feedback at scale, prototype concepts, improve the data developer experience, generate insights from data, and accelerate delivery without compromising quality.
Understanding customers and users: Spend time with municipal decision-makers and healthcare professionals to understand needs, build trusted relationships, and ensure data products get adopted and create value.
Communicate direction and progress: Collaborate closely with leadership and internal stakeholders (product, tech, compliance, sales/tender), and clearly prioritize needs we uncover in discovery and tender commitments in the product roadmap.
Lead the cross-functional D&A team day-to-day and make the build/buy and tooling trade-offs together with the team.
🤝 Who you are
This is first and foremost a Product Manager role, but we need someone with a data background who can be hands-on when needed and lead by example in what it means to be data-driven, both for Aidn and for the municipalities.
You likely have:
5+ years of experience from a data analyst role or similar, with an analytical mindset and a good understanding of what it takes to succeed with analytics.
Experience as a Product Manager (or equivalent product leadership), with a strong product mindset, or
Experience owning a data platform or internal data product, and driving change in how teams own and publish data (governance, self-service, or similar), ideally across teams you didn’t manage.
Strong business understanding and the ability to connect data to customer and company value.
Hands-on customer and user discovery experience, with the ability to uncover the underlying need behind a requested solution.
Experience working with non-technical users, and have strong communication and stakeholder management skills.
Practical experience using AI in both analytics and product work, and have opinions on how this should be applied in analytics.
Ability to set direction and lead in an ambiguous, fast-changing environment, and to lead through influence across teams.
Ability to be hands-on in data (SQL, modern data tooling) when needed.
Fluent Norwegian (C1 level) for collaboration and testing with municipal users, and professional English for internal collaboration.
It’s a plus if you have:
Experience driving distributed or federated data ownership, data mesh, or enablement models
Experience with dbt or similar transformation tooling and a modern self-service BI tool
B2B SaaS and scale-up experience
Healthtech, public sector, or another high-trust/regulated data environment
Familiarity with data governance and privacy considerations (e.g., DPIA).
👋 The Team
You will join our Data & Analytics team, a newly established cross-functional team with a data engineer, a UX designer, two developers (including a tech lead), and a Data Analyst. The team owns the shared data platform, the analytics capabilities, and the overall Aidn Analytics experience. The team operates as its own product area and works closely with several product teams and our Infrastructure team.
Problems we’re working on right now include:
Building a modern data platform from a blank slate, in a year when AI is reshaping what the interface for insight work looks like
Shaping how municipal care leadership makes decisions, so municipalities are prepared for rising demand and complexity in the services they must provide (the ageing population wave)
Experimenting with AI and agents to make data more accessible and understandable, within a distributed ownership model across our product organization, while onboarding many of Norway's municipalities.
💬 What success looks like
After 3 months:
Ramped up on Aidn's domain, data model, tender commitments, and municipal customers, and has met key municipalities and domain teams.
Has a clear view of what must be delivered fast, what can wait, and what moves to 2028.
Has built a few data products end-to-end with successful adoption in municipalities, with a good understanding of our platform and tooling.
After 6 months:
Owns and has communicated a clear direction for Aidn Analytics, including the plan for distributed ownership and the learnings from the first municipal users.
Multiple teams run according to distributed ownership, each with at least one data product delivered to real municipal users.
Feedback loops on data quality are in place. Internal use of the data platform is growing towards the 2027 targets.
After 12 months:
Distributed ownership works in practice, with most product teams building their own data products, and new teams can self-onboard using documentation and AI-assisted tooling.
Adoption is visible among municipalities, and Aidn Analytics is a reason municipalities choose and stay with Aidn.
A clear direction for Aidn Analytics across our products is defined, and delivery has started.
💙 Why you’ll love working here
High trust, real ownership
You’ll join a team with the freedom to explore challenging problems and own the results.
Visible impact
Your work will directly affect how healthcare professionals and municipalities across Norway do their jobs every day.
No legacy
You'll join a newly established team with no legacy, and the freedom to build great Data and Analytics experiences for our product teams and municipalities.
AI as a core tool
You'll actively incorporate AI into your work — experimenting with agentic tools, automating parts of your workflow, and helping define what responsible AI use looks like in Data & Analytics.

6 weeks vacation
Flexible working hours and location
Health & wellness benefit
Employee shares

A collaborative, ambitious, and caring team.

title: Data Analyst
description:
📍 Oslo / Bergen / Bodø

🌍 Why this role matters
Aidn has become the market leader in Norway's municipal healthcare sector, and municipalities across the country are now onboarding to our platform. That gives us something few companies have: the chance to change how an entire sector understands and uses its own data.
Today, most municipalities lack accessible, trustworthy insight into their own operational and clinical data. At the same time, they are facing an aging population that will put more pressure on their services every year. Good decisions will matter more than ever, and good decisions need good data.
Aidn Analytics is core to what we offer, but we are still early in defining what it will become. Whoever takes this role will help shape it from the ground up, at a time when AI is changing what insight work even looks like.
🔧 What you’ll be working on
As our Data Analyst, you will help Aidn and the municipalities make better decisions. You will build data products as part of your everyday work, and at the same time help set the standard for how data products get built across Aidn.
Your core responsibilities will include:
Building and maintaining analytics: Build the reports, dashboards, self-service tools, and data exports that municipalities and teams at Aidn rely on every day, with conversational analytics as an emerging capability.
Define what we measure: Define metrics and balanced quality and performance indicators for municipalities and for Aidn internally.
Working with municipalities: Work directly with municipal leadership and staff to translate operational and strategic questions into data products, and follow up until those products have the intended impact.
Strengthening data literacy: both at Aidn and in the municipalities, by developing capabilities and training that enable users to be self-served and create value from our data products.
Setting the standard for how data products get built, including improving the developer experience supported by AI. Enabling others to build according to our best practices.
Supporting product teams and helping them move towards distributed data ownership where they create data products within their domain for internal and external purposes
Contributing to platform work, tooling adoption and the shared developer experience for insights work, and embedding in product teams when they need hands-on support
🤝Who you are
We hire for attitude as much as for aptitude. Curiosity, ownership, and a collaborative spirit matter more than ticking every box.
That said, you’ll thrive here if you:
3+ years of experience in a data analyst role or similar, with an analytical mindset and a good understanding of what it takes to succeed with analytics.
A strong analytical mindset, turning vague questions into answers that change decisions. You ask good questions and work in a structured way with data, while thinking creatively and pragmatically about how we meet user needs. This is one of the most important qualities we’re looking for.
Write SQL independently at an advanced level, and have experience with modern data platforms (such as Databricks or Snowflake) and related tooling (such as dbt).

Experience from a product organisation, working in cross-functional teams where data products are built, shipped, and continuously improved.
Have built data products that people actually use in decision-making, and improved them over time.
A delivery-oriented, pragmatic approach, and the ability to take ownership and work independently in an ambiguous, fast-changing environment.
Fluent Norwegian (C1 level) for collaboration and testing with municipal users, and professional English for internal collaboration.

How do we help municipal care leaders move towards insight-based decisions, at both the strategic and operational levels, before the aging population wave hits?

title: Product Manager - Identity & Access Management (IAM)
description:
📍 Oslo / Bergen / Bodø / Remote
💰 Salary: 1.150.000 - 1.300.000 NOK/year
🌍 Why this role matters
Healthcare professionals need timely access to information to deliver good care. Patients need to trust that their information is protected. At Aidn, we’re building digital healthcare services that make both possible.
Team IAM builds the identity and access management foundations used across Aidn. From signing in and managing users to deciding who can access patient information and recording how it is used, the team’s work shapes the everyday experience of healthcare professionals and municipal system administrators.
As Product Manager, you’ll set direction for this product area and help make secure, compliant access understandable and easy to use. You’ll work on difficult questions with real consequences: How do we protect patient privacy while supporting care? How can municipalities manage access confidently? And how should access work when AI agents act on behalf of users?
🔧 What you’ll be working on
You’ll own the IAM product direction and roadmap, working closely with a Service Designer and Tech Lead in a product trio. Together, you’ll discover the right problems to solve, test ideas and follow their impact through to everyday use.
Your work will include:
Understanding customers and users. Spend time with municipal decision-makers, system administrators and healthcare professionals to understand their different needs, workflows and constraints.
Setting clear priorities. Turn discovery, company goals, regulatory requirements and technical realities into a coherent roadmap across authentication, authorization, user lifecycle, provisioning, organization management and access logging.
Making complexity usable. Help municipalities manage users and access with greater confidence and independence, while enabling healthcare professionals to reach the information they need.
Building and learning with AI. Create working prototypes to test assumptions, use AI in research and analysis, and help the team adopt effective practices while protecting sensitive information.
Connecting teams and requirements. Work with product teams, Platform, security and regulatory specialists to clarify ownership, coordinate dependencies and translate complex requirements into product decisions.
Owning outcomes after launch. Define success measures before delivery, follow up on rollout and use product data and user feedback to keep improving. You’ll also support municipal implementations and contribute IAM expertise to tender responses.
Current challenges include relationship-based access to patient records using OpenFGA, detecting potential misuse through audit logs, and developing access controls and audit trails for AI agents.
🤝 Who you are
You enjoy getting to the heart of complex problems and making them understandable to others. You’re curious, pragmatic and comfortable making decisions when the answer isn’t obvious. You raise risks and disagreements early, listen carefully and change direction when the evidence calls for it.
You bring:
Product management experience in a technical product area with at least 3–5 years of ownership spanning discovery, prioritization, delivery, rollout and iteration. We welcome candidates at different levels of seniority.
Working knowledge of identity and access management, including authentication, authorization, access-control models, single sign-on, user lifecycle, provisioning and auditability.
Hands-on customer and user discovery experience, with the ability to uncover the underlying need behind a requested solution.
Experience defining meaningful outcomes and using qualitative and quantitative evidence to improve products after launch.
Practical experience using AI in everyday product work, including building working prototypes and helping others adopt useful approaches.
Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to align customers, engineers, designers and specialists around priorities and trade-offs.
Fluent Norwegian for research and testing with municipal users, and professional English for internal collaboration.
It’s a plus if you have:
Experience in healthcare or another regulated environment.
Familiarity with Norwegian healthcare requirements, such as Normen, pasientjournalloven or HelseID guidance.
Deeper knowledge of APIs, OAuth 2.0/OpenID Connect, Entra ID, SCIM or access-control architecture.
Experience with multi-tenant products, public-sector customers, municipal onboarding or tenders.
You’ll need enough technical understanding to explore solutions and make sound product decisions with engineers. Writing production code is not part of the role.
👋 Your team
Team IAM is a cross-functional team in Aidn’s Platform domain, with colleagues in Oslo, Trondheim and Bodø. You’ll work with a shared Service Designer, a Tech Lead and engineers specializing in backend and full-stack development.
In the product trio, you’ll take responsibility for customer value and business viability, alongside your design and engineering partners. Together, you’ll shape shared foundations that every Aidn product area depends on.
💬 What success looks like
In 3 months, you understand the main IAM services, user needs and regulatory context. You’ve built relationships with your team and municipal and internal stakeholders, and your discovery work is helping shape priorities.
In 6 months, you’ve established a clear product direction and helped launch or improve a capability with measurable user impact. You’re using AI prototypes to test assumptions, and important cross-team dependencies have clear ownership.
In 12 months, discovery, measurement and learning after launch are established parts of how the team works. The IAM roadmap is understood across teams and balances customer needs, company goals, regulation and technical sustainability.
💙 Why you’ll love working here
Meaningful impact. Help protect patient privacy and give healthcare professionals access to information that supports better care.
High trust, real ownership. Join an empowered team with the freedom to explore difficult problems and responsibility for the results.
Room to grow. Build deep expertise in healthcare identity and access management, influence product decisions across Aidn and help shape emerging areas such as access for AI agents.

Flexible working hours and location

Employee shares

A collaborative, ambitious and caring team

title: Tech Lead
description:
Vil du være Tech Lead i et av våre smoothe produktteam? 🏎️
Om oss 🚗
Siden starten i 2017 har Nettbil gjort bilsalg enklere og tryggere for privatpersoner ved å la flere bilforhandlere konkurrere om samme bil. Over 100 000 biler er solgt gjennom plattformen vår, til mer enn 2 000 forhandlere.
Vi er en del av Vend, den største markedsplass-operatøren i Norden. Med fokus på å utnytte teknologi og forbedre brukeropplevelsen er Nettbil et av de mest spennende vekstselskapene i Norge. Hos oss er kultur nøkkelen: Vi jobber sammen, vi er sultne på å lykkes, og vi finner smarte løsninger.
Om rollen 🧑‍💻
Bak det som for kundene virker friksjonsfritt, ligger et kraftfullt maskineri. Vi gjør handelen enkel for begge parter: bileieren som skal selge, og forhandleren som skal kjøpe. Det krever team som både bygger godt og jobber godt sammen.
Nettbil vokser, og vi bygger ut flere produktteam med tydelige ansvarsområder. Derfor ser vi etter en Tech Lead som vil være med og forme teknologien, teamet og veien videre.
Tech Lead rapporterer direkte til CTO og er en del av Technology, der alle jobber eller har jobbet hands-on med teknologi. Rollen kombinerer det å skrive kode med ansvaret for å utvikle og lede menneskene i teamet.
Som Tech Lead vil du blant annet:
Lede teamets utviklere, både faglig og som personalleder
Bryte ned komplekse problemstillinger og ta tekniske veivalg sammen med teamet
Utfordre etablerte løsninger og finne smartere måter å bygge på
Være sparringspartner for Product Manager og koble teknologi og forretningsbehov sammen
Samarbeide med andre Tech Leads om avhengigheter, standarder og prinsipper på tvers
Bygge et team der folk trives og lykkes sammen
Hvem er du? 🌟
Du har solid erfaring som utvikler og har tatt steget inn i ledelse uten å legge fra deg koden. Du trives med å få folk til å lykkes og tar like mye eierskap til hvordan teamet har det som til hva dere leverer. Du gir ærlig og tydelig feedback, forventer det samme tilbake og sier fra når noe er på vei i feil retning. Når noe feiler, er du opptatt av hva vi kan lære, ikke hvem som har skylden.
Vi ser etter deg som:
Har minst 5 års erfaring som utvikler og fortsatt skriver kode jevnlig
Har erfaring med teknisk ledelse av et team
Har ledet utviklere, inkludert personalledelse
Har relevant utdanning eller tilsvarende bakgrunn
Behersker norsk som arbeidsspråk
Trives med å jobbe tett med kolleger på kontoret vårt på Økern
Teknologistacken vår 🚦
Hos oss får du være med på å modernisere teknologiplattformen vår for videre vekst. Har du gjort noe lignende før, er du godt skodd. Du trenger ikke å være ekspert på alle teknologiene våre. Det viktigste er at du har solid teknisk forståelse og ser helheten.
Dette er noe av det du kan forvente hos Nettbil:
Språk: TypeScript
Backend: Node.js
Databaser: PostgreSQL, MySQL
Infrastruktur: AWS, Kubernetes, OpenTofu
Køer: BullMQ
Testing: Cypress, Vitest
Frontend: React Router, TanStack Query, Tailwind
Vi har også teknologi utenfor listen over. Blant annet forvaltes innholdet vårt i Sanity (med Next.js), og til analyse og maskinlæring bruker vi Redshift og SageMaker, med innslag av språk som Python og Go. Datadog gir oss observerbarhet på tvers av tjenestene.
Hva vi kan tilby deg 🌞
En sentral rolle i videreutviklingen av teknologien vår, med stor frihet og korte beslutningsveier
Et inkluderende arbeidsmiljø preget av samarbeid, høy faglig kompetanse og felles ambisjoner
Farten og mulighetene i en scale-up, kombinert med tryggheten og støtten fra Vend-konsernet
Gode muligheter til å vokse både faglig og som leder
Moderne kontorlokaler med treningssenter, takterrasse og flere lunsjsteder
Konkurransedyktige betingelser og gode pensjons- og forsikringsordninger
Hos Nettbil blir du en del av et sammensveiset og engasjert miljø med rundt 100 kollegaer. Vi tror at de beste løsningene skapes når mennesker med ulike erfaringer og perspektiver samarbeider, og legger derfor stor vekt på kunnskapsdeling, samarbeid og utvikling.
Vi holder til i toppetasjen på Økern Portal med utsikt over hele Oslo, takterrasse, treningssenter i bygget og flere gode lunsjsteder. Det er likevel menneskene som gjør arbeidsplassen vår spesiell. Vi har en kultur med lav terskel for å dele ideer, hjelpe hverandre og feire små og store milepæler. Enten det er sommerfest, felles lunsjer eller sosiale samlinger, jobber vi for å skape en ambisiøs arbeidsplass der det er både meningsfylt og hyggelig å være.
Slik søker du 🧰
Send oss CV og noen ord om deg selv og hva som motiverer deg for rollen. Søknader vurderes fortløpende. Har du spørsmål om stillingen eller ønsker en uforpliktende prat, er du velkommen til å ta kontakt med Martine Grønlund på [email removed].
⭐ Vi er stolte av tilliten kundene våre viser oss med 4,8 av 5 stjerner på Trustpilot!

Data Engineering
Dette er rollen for deg som evner å forstå forretningsbehov, oversette dem til robuste dataarkitekturer og levere innsikt gjennom brukervennlige rapporter og visualiseringer. Etablere og forbedre DataOps-prosesser, inkludert CI/CD, Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Bicep eller tilsvarende), versjonskontroll og monitorering
Data Science
Dette er rollen for deg som brenner for å utforske data og utvikle prediktive og analytiske modeller som skaper reell forretningsverdi.

Trene og evaluere maskinlærings- og statistiske modeller – fra eksperimentering og hypotesetesting til å velge riktig tilnærming for problemet
Utforske og analysere store datasett for å avdekke mønstre, anomalier og muligheter som ikke er åpenbare på forhånd
Designe og kjøre A/B-tester og eksperimenter for å validere hypoteser og måle effekt av tiltak
Bygge og forbedre feature engineering-pipelines i samarbeid med data engineers for å gjøre data modellklare
Bygge og videreutvikle AI- og maskinlæringsmodeller på moderne plattformer

Du har forståelse for arkitekturer innen datavarehus, lakehouse og ELT/ETL-prosesser
Det er en fordel om du har erfaring med BI-verktøy som Power BI, Qlik eller lignende

title: Business Development Manager
description:
Business Development Manager – Industrial Cybersecurity
A security digital twin company
Omny is on a mission to protect critical infrastructure from cyber disruption. With visibility from IT systems to the factory floor, we leverage the latest advancements in data science to identify and protect our customers assets from these threats. By bringing together asset owners, technology providers, engineering companies, and security specialists on a shared digital foundation, we're changing how industrial cybersecurity is managed. Now, we're looking for experienced a Business Developer Manager who will play a central role in driving Omny's commercial growth by identifying, developing, and converting customer opportunities into long-term business relationships. Omny is uniquely headquartered in Norway with an international team and vision.
Role Overview
The Business Development Manager will play a central role in driving Omny's commercial growth by identifying, developing, and converting customer opportunities into long-term business relationships.
This role combines strategic business development, consultative sales, and project-based execution. The successful candidate will work closely with industrial customers to understand their operations, business processes, and value chains, identify critical challenges, and translate these into concrete opportunities where Omny's platform can deliver measurable business value.
A key responsibility will be to break down complex industrial value chains and operational challenges into clearly defined customer use cases, business value propositions, and commercially actionable opportunities.
The role requires a structured and analytical approach to problem-solving, combined with strong stakeholder management, facilitation skills, and the ability to drive initiatives forward in iterative cycles. The Business Development Manager will engage with stakeholders across business, operations, IT, OT, and cybersecurity, aligning different perspectives around shared priorities and measurable outcomes.
Role & Responsibilities
Strategic Business Development & Value Creation
Identify, develop, and close commercial opportunities across Omny's target industries, including Oil & Gas, Manufacturing, Utilities, Defence, and Transportation.
Analyze customers' operational processes and value chains to identify business challenges and translate them into actionable use cases and measurable customer value.
Develop compelling business cases and value propositions, translating technical capabilities into clear commercial and operational outcomes.
Build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders, understanding their strategic priorities and positioning Omny as a long-term partner.
Consultative Sales & Commercial Execution
Own the full sales cycle, from prospecting and customer discovery to proposals, negotiations, and closing, with accountability for commercial results.
Lead customer workshops and discovery processes to validate needs, develop solutions, and progress commercial opportunities.
Apply an iterative, hypothesis-driven approach to refining customer value propositions and developing new business.
Build and manage a qualified sales pipeline, ensuring structured follow-up, opportunity progression, and long-term account development.
Project Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration
Lead cross-functional initiatives involving customers, internal teams, and external partners, ensuring alignment and effective execution.

title: Are you our new Cloud Engineer?
description:
A security digital twin company
Omny is on a mission to protect critical infrastructure from cyber disruption. With visibility from IT systems to the factory floor, we leverage the latest advancements in data science to identify and protect customers assets from these threats. By bringing together asset owners, technology providers, engineering companies, and security specialists on a shared digital foundation, we're changing how industrial cybersecurity is managed. Now, we're looking for an experienced Cloud Engineer.
Omny is uniquely headquartered in Norway with an international team and vision.
What will you do?

Design, implement, and manage cloud infrastructure on Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
Develop and maintain infrastructure as code using Terraform, including module development and state management.
Build, maintain, and optimize CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions to support reliable and automated deployments.
Monitor, troubleshoot, and optimize platform performance, availability, and cloud resource usage.
Participate in incident response, root cause analysis, and post-mortem reviews to improve system reliability.
Collaborate closely with software developers to support application deployments and infrastructure requirements.
Contribute to internal tooling, automation, and infrastructure documentation.
Evaluate and recommend new tools, services, and technologies to improve the platform and engineering workflows.

Strong experience with infrastructure as code, including module design, state management, and testing.
Solid understanding of cloud infrastructure fundamentals, including compute, networking, identity and access management (IAM), storage, and managed services.

Experience with coding for automation, tooling, and testing.
Hands-on experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines.
Strong knowledge of cloud networking concepts, including VPCs, firewalls, load balancers, and DNS.
Strong security awareness, including IAM best practices, least-privilege principles, and secrets management.
Excellent English written and verbal communication skills.

The following experience is considered beneficial but not required:
Experience working with multi-cloud environments, including AWS or Azure in addition to GCP.
Familiarity with container orchestration platforms, such as Kubernetes (GKE) or OpenShift.
Experience with private cloud or hybrid cloud environments.
What you value
Motivated by a start-up environment in a flexible and rapidly evolving organization
Interested to learn about cyber security in industrial control systems

Proactiveness and a willingness to dive into problem solving
Ability to embrace uncertainty, daring to try new things and learning from mistakes along the way
Curious and open minded, approaching everything with a willingness to learn

title: OT Security Specialist
description:
Omny is expanding its Professional Services team and looking for OT Security Specialists who want to go beyond traditional consulting.
In this role, you will work hands-on with the Omny Platform to deliver end-to-end customer value. You will help industrial organizations gain full visibility into their OT infrastructure, understand what their most critical assets are and how to protect them from cyber threats.
Through Omny Platform, you will enable them to continuously monitor their security maturity and compliance status, their risk posture and help them prioritize security measures to remove gaps and vulnerabilities. Instead of building one-off reports or static assessments, you will help customers operationalize security through a scalable and dynamic platform that provides measurable, long lasting value to Security and Operations teams.
With this role, you have an opportunity to shape your career as Omny grows into the trusted cybersecurity partner for industrial enterprises globally. Not only that, you will use your expertise and experience to directly impact and shape the future of our Omny Platform, its capabilities and the value it unlocks for our customers.
What You’ll Do
Work directly with industrial customers to map their OT environments, assess risks, and improve cybersecurity posture.
Use the Omny Platform to perform security assessments and enable customers to run them independently in the future.
Conduct reviews of ICS/OT networks, identifying vulnerabilities and opportunities for improvement.
Collaborate closely with Product and Engineering to continuously improve Omny Platform
Conduct demonstrations of Omny Platform and its value to existing and prospective Customers and partners.
Travel to customer sites when needed (including offshore)
What You Bring
Solid experience with Operational Technology / Industrial Control Systems (SCADA, HMI, DCS, PLC).
Understanding of industrial network architectures (Purdue, NAMUR NOA).
Experience with OT risk, vulnerability, or gap assessments across large-scale industrial environments.
Familiarity with OT security technologies (incl. but not limited to network sensors, industrial firewalls, vulnerability management).
Knowledge of IEC 62443 and relevant governance and compliance frameworks.
Strong communication skills, especially in customer-facing settings.
Advantage With:
Experience with incident response planning in industrial environments
Norwegian language proficiency at C1 level.
More About Omny
Omny is an industrial cybersecurity SaaS scale-up founded by Telenor, Aker ASA, and Cognite. Our mission is to secure the operational resilience of critical infrastructure by bridging the long-standing gap between OT and IT security.
Our Omny Platform provides unified visibility across all Purdue levels (L0–L5), combining operational data, passive network scanning, enterprise and security architecture information, threat intelligence, and compliance requirements (e.g., NIS2, IEC 62443, NIST CSF 2.0). Leveraging our deep OT domain expertise and Cognite Data Fusion as our powerful data platform backbone, Omny enables organizations to identify and implement the most impactful security measures and to respond to cyber incidents decisively and with clear focus.
Headquartered in Oslo, with presence in Stavanger and global ambitions, Omny is addressing critical infrastructure organisations across O&G, Manufacturing, Energy & Power, Pharma, and Chemicals.
